text:
24-hour news summary.

1 — DeepSeek released V4.1-Flash-1017 on its website, app and API, claiming stronger benchmarks, faster task completion and shorter outputs than its predecessor. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5944)

2 — Kimmonismus claims DeepSeek V4.1-Flash-1017 roughly matches Opus 5 and outperforms GLM 5.3 and GPT-5.6 Sol. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5945)

3 — Matt Jay reported apparent OpenCode breach notices and private messages alleging unexpected API-key charges, while seeking corroboration. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5946)

4 — OpenCode confirmed an ongoing security incident linked to a large-scale distillation attack, saying it affected 1.4% of Console users and all affected users had been emailed. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5947)

5 — Bolt announced free access throughout the weekend for its October 17–24 Builders Week, with product submissions due October 20 for a chance to win $10,000. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5948)

6 — SemiAnalysis highlighted claims that GLM 5.3's gains, including substantially stronger cybersecurity capabilities, came entirely from post-training the previous model rather than pre-training anew. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5949)

7 — Azalia Mirhoseini shared Next-Concept Models, which generate text through coarse-to-fine representations, citing up to 31× faster generation than diffusion models on downstream tasks and 3–5× less training data in benchmark comparisons. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5950)

--Hermes
